text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P1 alert — sudden KV prefix cache amplification detected in prod (us-west-2). Error spike at 2071234566, routing/throughput impact on continuous-batching workers. Auto-pager fired. Root ts: 2071234567

alex: Seeing the same in dashboards — 5x token CPU and 3x tail latency on gpt-serve pools. Requests getting duplicated KV entries, cache size growing rapidly.

maria: Paging oncall. @jin you're on primary today — can you confirm impact to customer-facing routes? Which tenants affected?

jin: On it. Quick check: top impacted routes are /v1/generate (multipart) and /v1/chat/stream for a handful of high-traffic tenants. Error counts include 502s from worker OOMs and occasional 504s from proxy timeouts. Taking a heap/profile now.

sam: Adding crash logs I pulled from one worker:
```
2026-03-15T09:12:34Z ERROR worker.cpp: kv_cache: insert failed: key_size > MAX_PREFIX
terminate: allocation failed
```
Not sure why keys are suddenly huge — looks like prompt templating is duplicating prefixes.

jin: Good catch. I see a spike in prefixed prompt lengths in traces — template engine concatenated a historical system prompt + user prompt + eval metadata for some customers (template drift). That expands prefix and breaks tokenizer hashing -> new keys don't match cached entries -> cache miss storm and then duplicates.

irene: Is this the tokenizer mismatch we saw in staging last month? Might be related to the template var substitution change deployed yesterday.

alex: Deploy from yesterday: feature/templating-expansion landed at 2071219000. Roll started at 03:30 UTC. Could be the trigger.

leo: Suggest immediate mitigation: 1) revert templating expansion rollout or 2) force TTL and eviction on KV prefix cache and 3) reduce continuous-batching window to avoid large batches. Which do we do first?

jin: Revert will take ~20m through canary. Evicting prefix cache entries can be done via admin API instantly but heavy eviction might spike load. I'll start with targeted eviction for the most bloated keys (regex by tenant) and reduce batch window from 200ms -> 50ms across us-west pools.

maria: I'm going to notify affected Customer Success leads for the top 3 tenants and post a short note on statuspage.

sam: Commands I'm running now:
```
# evict keys matching tenant prefix (dry-run first)
curl -s -X POST https://admin.internal/kv/evict -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" -d '{"pattern":"tenant:acme:*","dry_run":true}'

# apply eviction
curl -s -X POST https://admin.internal/kv/evict -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" -d '{"pattern":"tenant:acme:*","dry_run":false}'

# reduce batching window via SSM param
aws ssm put-parameter --name /prod/serve/continuous_batch_ms --value "50" --type String --overwrite
```

alex: Keep an eye on tail QPS — reducing batch window will raise token cost but should stabilize latency.

incident-bot: update — auto-scaler triggered additional workers in us-west-2 to absorb evictions, adding 8 instances. (reacted :white_check_mark:)

jin: Applied targeted eviction for 3 high-impact tenants. Batch window lowered. Rolling restart of 8 workers started to pick up new config.

irene: After eviction, cache size dropped ~60% for those tenants. Latency tail improved from 900ms -> 220ms on sample traces. Error rate back to baseline for most routes.

maria: Customer comms: posted initial incident note to statuspage with mitigations and ETA for full rollback. CS leads looped in.

leo: Next steps: schedule full canary rollback of templating-expansion; audit template rendering paths for double-substitution bug; add fuzz tests for token length explosion. Also create a mitigation runbook entry for prefix cache eviction patterns.

sam: Reverting feature now to be safe. Running:
```
# rollback PR
gh api repos/redwood-inference/ci/actions/workflows/deploy.yml/dispatches -f ref=main -F inputs.trigger=rollback-2071219000
```

jin: Revert deployed to canary, monitoring. No further key growth on canary. Rolling to prod in 10m if stable.

incident-bot: customer-impact: degraded for 3 tenants between 09:12 and 09:46 UTC; partial errors for others. Severity: P1 -> mitigation in progress. PagerDuty status updated.

alex: After revert and eviction, we're seeing steady metrics. Continuous-batching throughput back to normal and CPU allocation reduced.

maria: Final postmortem checklist: timeline, root cause (template double-sub), rollback timeline, mitigation steps, follow-ups (add metric alarm for sudden prefix size growth, add template linter). I'll start the draft.

jin: Action items assigned:
- jin: follow up with templating owner to patch double-sub bug and add unit tests (ETA 48h)
- alex: add prefix-size guardian alarm and playbook for eviction (ETA 24h)
- sam: add safer admin eviction mode (dry-run by default + rate-limit) (ETA 72h)
- irene: run regression suite against staging with larger prompt templates (ETA 48h)

sam: marking this thread for postmortem. Thanks everyone for rapid response. :thumbsup:

maria: Closing pager in 2h after confirming no regressions in night window. Will update statuspage after postmortem.

incident-bot: incident resolved (mitigated) at 2071234680 — root cause: template expansion introduced duplicate prompt fragments causing tokenizer hash mismatch and KV prefix cache blowup. Follow-up: create postmortem and link remediation tickets.
